summary.text: Mike Klein, a West Point graduate and Army combat veteran with no party affiliation, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Florida's 3rd Congressional District to Kat Cammack.
A fifth-generation Floridian raised in Gainesville, he served in the U.S. Army from 1985 to 2003 and is chairman of Warrior Centric Health.

paragraphs.text: According to his campaign survey, Klein is a fifth-generation Floridian who was raised in Gainesville in the 1970s.
He graduated from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point in 1989 and later earned a graduate degree from the University of South Carolina's Darla Moore School of Business.
Klein served in the U.S. Army from 1985 to 2003; he says he was a Ranger-qualified Infantry officer in the 25th Infantry Division who led soldiers in combat in Operation Desert Storm.
Klein says he has worked and lived internationally, building expertise in international business, economic development, university innovation and entrepreneurship.

He co-founded and chairs Warrior Centric Health, which he says works to improve care for the military and veteran community; he says he started it after his brother, an Army infantry officer, lost limbs to an IED.
Klein ran as an independent. He describes himself as the father of two "Gators" and says he has pledged not to take corporate PAC or special-interest money.
During the campaign, he emphasized removing corporate and special-interest money from politics.
He received 1.9% of the vote to Kat Cammack's 55.1%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
